document.name: PrismSpace Agent Swarm Architecture
document.purpose: Explain the project architecture with exclusive focus on Multi Agent Orchestration through the Agent Swarm tool.

redaction_policy.rule: The requested product/runtime name is omitted from this document. Backend paths and environment keys that contain that name are represented with neutral aliases.

included: Telemetry, logs, evaluation, and training direction for orchestration

project.name: PrismSpace Multi Agent Orchestration
project.focus: Agent Swarm is the primary project surface for launching, monitoring, routing, validating, and improving multi-agent workflows.
project.architecture_style: Next.js frontend plus API proxy plus local Python orchestration backend
project.primary_capability: Convert a user objective into a managed agent run with configurable model routing, worker count, approval checkpoints, live logs, and final synthesis.

project_description.one_line_summary: PrismSpace is a local AI workspace whose central architecture focus is Agent Swarm: a Multi Agent Orchestration system that turns user objectives into observable, approval-aware, model-routed agent runs.
project_description.full_description: The project combines a modern browser-based React interface with a local Python backend bridge so a user can launch multi-agent work from the PrismSpace UI, choose a model provider, limit worker count, decide whether a human checkpoint is required, watch execution logs in real time, approve or reject paused work, and inspect the final synthesized answer. The Agent Swarm feature is not treated as a generic utility panel; it is the orchestration layer of the application and the part of the system intended to coordinate planning, routing, tool awareness, execution, validation, and feedback collection.

product_identity.intended_runtime: Local-first development environment with browser UI and local backend service
product_identity.target_user: A developer, researcher, designer, or technical operator who wants to delegate complex objectives to a coordinated set of AI agents while still being able to inspect, approve, and control the run.
product_identity.core_value: Make autonomous AI work visible, configurable, and controllable instead of sending a prompt into a black box.

what_the_project_does: Accepts natural-language objectives from the user.
Routes those objectives into the Agent Swarm launch flow.
Creates a tracked agent run with a unique id.
Stores run metadata including objective, model, provider, worker count, approval state, status, timestamps, and result.
Builds a system prompt that frames the selected model as a multi-agent coordinator.
Injects live MCP server and credential awareness into the orchestration context when available.
Simulates and logs the planning and worker-spawn stages of a multi-agent run.
Pauses for human approval when human-in-the-loop mode is enabled.
Calls the selected provider/model after planning and approval requirements are satisfied.
Streams logs back to the UI through Server-Sent Events.
Stores the final response on the agent run object.
Lets the user review historical and active runs.
Lets the user delete run records from the current backend registry.
Exposes masked MCP credential state and lets users save or remove tokens for orchestration tools.
what_the_project_is_not: It is not documented here as a general collection of developer tools.
It is not focused here on unrelated productivity widgets, static tools, or dashboard customization features.
It is not a replacement for individual LLM providers; it is an orchestration layer above them.
It is not yet a fully persistent production agent platform because current run state is held in memory.

frontend.styling: Tailwind CSS with component-level React UI

backend.state_management: In-memory dictionaries for agent state and logs
backend.configuration: Environment variables and local MCP server configuration files

model_providers.selection_pattern: The user selects provider and model in the UI; the backend dispatches to the matching async provider helper.

tool_awareness.purpose: Expose configured tool servers and credentials to the orchestration prompt so Agent Swarm can reason about tool availability.
tool_awareness.credential_handling: Tokens are stored locally, masked in UI responses, and referenced by environment variable keys.

runtime_topology.browser: The user interacts with the Agent Swarm panel inside the Next.js app.
runtime_topology.next_app: The Next.js application renders the UI and exposes same-origin API routes under /api/agent-swarm.
runtime_topology.api_proxy: The Next.js API routes forward CRUD, health, approval, MCP, and SSE requests to the local Python backend.
runtime_topology.python_backend: The FastAPI service owns run state, log state, provider dispatch, MCP config loading, token update operations, and the background run lifecycle.
runtime_topology.llm_provider: The selected external model provider receives the orchestration system prompt, compact chat history, and user objective.
runtime_topology.mcp_config: Local MCP server definitions and token status are loaded into backend context and optionally surfaced to the UI.

steps: Open Agent Swarm.
Enter or receive a natural-language objective.
Select provider and model.
Choose worker count.
Enable or disable human checkpointing.
Submit the run.
Watch the run move from initialising to planning, running, and completed.
Submit a run with human checkpoint enabled.
Wait for the backend to enter awaiting_approval.
Inspect logs and intent.
Approve to resume or reject to cancel.
Continue watching logs until a terminal state is reached.
Open the Agent Swarm chat/run list.
Select an existing run.
Review objective, provider, model, status, logs, DAG view, and output.
Delete the run if it is no longer needed.
Open the MCP tab.
Refresh configured MCP servers.
Select a server or token key.
Save a local credential value.
Confirm that the UI reports the token as configured without exposing the raw secret.

agent_run.description: The core unit of work in Agent Swarm.

fields.id: Unique identifier generated by the backend.
fields.max_agents: The requested number of specialized workers.
fields.human_in_loop: Whether approval is required before final execution.
fields.result: Final provider response or error text.
fields.approved: Null before decision, true after approval, false after rejection.

log_entry.description: Timestamped text emitted by the backend to explain run progress.

mcp_server.description: A configured external tool server that can be described to the orchestration prompt.

mcp_token.description: A local environment-backed credential used by one or more MCP servers.

operational_details.backend_url_configuration: The Next.js proxy reads a backend URL environment variable and falls back to localhost:7433.
operational_details.sse_behavior: The logs route is force-dynamic and forwards text/event-stream responses from the backend.
operational_details.run_storage_lifetime: Runs last only as long as the backend process keeps its in-memory dictionaries.
operational_details.approval_timeout: The backend waits for approval for roughly 300 seconds before failing the run.
operational_details.chat_history_limit: The backend keeps up to the last 16 user/assistant messages and trims each message before provider calls.

design_principles: Keep orchestration observable through live logs and explicit statuses.
Keep autonomy bounded through provider choice, worker limits, and approval checkpoints.
Keep tool use grounded by loading real MCP server configuration instead of pretending tools exist.
Keep provider access replaceable by routing through provider-specific backend helpers.
Keep the browser client simple by using typed helper functions and same-origin proxy routes.
Keep future training possible by treating each run as telemetry for intent routing, model routing, validation, and reward learning.

partially_implemented: DAG planning is represented in logs but not yet as a persisted executable graph.
Specialized sub-agents are represented in the orchestration prompt and logs but not yet tracked as independent runtime entities.
Validation is logged but not yet represented as structured pass/fail checks.
Model routing is user-selected rather than policy-learned.
Tool routing is prompt-informed by MCP configuration but not yet executed as a structured orchestration graph.

backend_bridge.name: Agent Swarm backend bridge
backend_bridge.actual_role: FastAPI service that stores run state, emits logs, handles approvals, builds orchestration prompts, and calls selected LLM providers.

state.agents: In-memory dictionary keyed by agent id.
state.logs: In-memory list of timestamped log lines keyed by agent id.
state.production_note: The current store is volatile and should be replaced with persistent storage for production runs.

status_flow.meaning: The run has been created and queued as a background task.
The backend logs DAG compilation and prepares specialized workers.
If human-in-the-loop is enabled, the run pauses until an operator approves or rejects it.
The backend sends the objective, compact chat history, and orchestration system prompt to the selected provider/model.
The model response has been received, validation logs have been emitted, and the final result is stored.
The run raised an error, timed out at approval, or hit an unsupported provider.
The operator rejected the run at the approval checkpoint.

happy_path: User submits objective in Agent Swarm
UI builds CreateAgentPayload with objective, provider, model, max_agents, human_in_loop, and chat_history
Next.js proxy forwards to backend POST /api/agents
Backend creates an agent id and stores initial state
Backend starts a background run task
UI selects the new agent and subscribes to GET /api/agent-swarm/agents/:id/logs
Backend emits planning, worker, approval, provider call, validation, and completion logs
UI updates logs and final output as the run reaches a terminal state

backend_behavior: Wait up to roughly 300 seconds for approval state
ui_behavior: Expose approve/reject controls for paused runs

current_gaps_and_recommendations.current: UI clamps visible worker count to 1 through 3.

current_gaps_and_recommendations.current: Approval is a single checkpoint before final execution.
